page_title: BBC Learning English - English at Work / Room 301
title: Room 301
description:
The boss isn't happy with Tom! But Anna is told 'Well done!' Find out what words he uses to give Anna the praise she deserves...
This episode explores language for giving praise.
phrases: You were in a difficult situation and you handled it well.

listening_challenge.question: In which country is the big boss of Tip Top Trading based?
listening_challenge.answer:
In which country is the 'big boss' of Tip Top Trading based?
America / United States

transcript.speaker: Paul
transcript.text: Good afternoon.

transcript.speaker: Anna & Tom
transcript.text: Hi, good afternoon.

transcript.speaker: Paul
transcript.text: Anna, Tom, room 301 please. Now.

transcript.speaker: Narrator
transcript.text: Welcome back to Tip Top Trading, where things are a teeny bit tense today. Paul has called Tom and Anna into room 301, the place where difficult conversations happen. Perhaps Paul has found out about yesterday's unhappy clients.

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: Oh dear.

transcript.speaker: Narrator
transcript.text: You should be okay Anna. After the way you coped with Mr Lime, you should be praised.

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: Really? What do you think Paul will say?

transcript.speaker: Narrator
transcript.text: Well, if he is pleased, he'll say things like:

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: And if he's not?

transcript.speaker: Narrator
transcript.text: Well, I suppose – oop. Here’s Paul now!

transcript.speaker: Paul
transcript.text: Well, Tom, Anna... Yesterday was not a great day. Two clients came in with serious complaints. Mrs Kumquat received a delivery of imitation bananas that were purple, not very convincing. And Mr Lime ordered grapefruits, but got pineapples. Tom.

transcript.speaker: Tom
transcript.text: Yes.

transcript.speaker: Paul
transcript.text: Were you responsible for these errors?

transcript.speaker: Tom
transcript.text: Well... yes, but…

transcript.speaker: Paul
transcript.text: Look, mistakes happen. But it seems that Mrs Kumquat left our offices even angrier than when she came in and she says she will never use Tip Top Trading again.

transcript.speaker: Tom
transcript.text: I tried my best.

transcript.speaker: Paul
transcript.text: Hmmm. I understand you told her to spray-paint the bananas and to 'stop being such a miserable old witch'.

transcript.speaker: Tom
transcript.text: Yeah, well look, she'd been very rude to me.

transcript.speaker: Paul
transcript.text: If you weren't such a good salesman I would fire you for that. Anna.

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: Yes.

transcript.speaker: Paul
transcript.text: Well done. Not only was Mr Lime satisfied that his problem would be resolved, but we might even get some extra business from him, thanks to your Imperial Lemon proposal.

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: I hope so.

transcript.speaker: Paul
transcript.text: You were in a difficult situation and you handled it well. You remained calm, friendly and professional. So, great job. I'm really impressed. I'm going to…
(phone rings)

transcript.speaker: Paul
transcript.text: Who's that? Oh no. It's a call from the USA.

transcript.speaker: Tom
transcript.text: Oh god!

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: What?

transcript.speaker: Tom
transcript.text: It's the boss!

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: Whose boss?

transcript.speaker: Tom
transcript.text: Ours! The big, big boss, based in America.

transcript.speaker: Paul
transcript.text: Shhhh! (on the phone) Hellooo? Ah, good afternoon Mr Socrates, I mean, er- morning, ha ha, where you are it's … yes, no, n-yes …. I'm not sure. Mrs Kumquat … did she? … well, it was very unfortunate …. purple, yes …. totally unacceptable …. I will. If you'd like I could …. Mr Socrates? Hello? Mr Socrates? Oh, he's gone. Right where was I? Tom, great work. Anna, I'm disappointed. No, no, Anna, great work, I want you to take charge of the Imperial Lemon presentation. Tom, if you speak to a client like that again there will be disciplinary action. Mrs Kumquat was so angry she even emailed Mr Socrates. Ok, that’s it.

transcript.speaker: Narrator
transcript.text: Phew! What a relief for Anna. Let's listen again to some of the phrases Paul used to praise her:
He also explained why he thought Anna had done a good job:
Excellent work Anna. But Tom's mistakes have given everyone a lot of work to do tomorrow.

transcript.speaker: Paul
transcript.text: First thing tomorrow we need to sort this mess out. Tom, I want you to phone every single client and check the orders. Anna, you can go to the warehouse and find out what's going on in there!
